newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Stals sees more frequent rate changes.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Stals sees more frequent rate changes.

text.p: South African central Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals said on Thursday he saw more frequent interest rate changes in future, adding a rate cut was possible if conditions improved in 1997.

Stals told state radio that the Reserve Bank was forced to increase its bank rate from 16 to 17 percent with effect from Thursday following a further increase in inflation and pressure on the financial markets over the past two weeks.

"With these very volatile capital movements in and out of the country we should in South Africa adapt ourselves to more frequent changes in interest rates and if the situation improves next year -- yes our interest rates are high -- at some stage it is possible that we can reduce interest rates again," Stals said in a radio interview.
Stals defended his move to hike rates.
"I think on the basis of the developments of the last two weeks and the further depreciation of the rand in October the increase in the bank rate has been justified," he added.
He said the one percentage point hike may be "bad news" in the short term.

"It is a basic problem of our economy that we are supporting our spending to a very large extent by borrowing money from banks...in the short term it may be bad news for economic growth but higher inflation next year will even be worse for economic growth in the medium to longer term," Stals said.
He added: "To fight inflation now will give us more growth and more opportunities to create more jobs in the medium and longer term".
